place: a crowded campus cafe in Bologna
who: two chemistry students
situation: Sofia checks the online results board and learns their group project won the best design prize. She rushes back to the table where Mateo is spilling coffee.

place: a quiet library stairwell in Edinburgh
who: a first-year student and his older sister
situation: Lucas whispers on his mobile because he accidentally locked his exam timetable inside his dorm locker. His sister reads the room number from a photo he sent yesterday.

place: a lecture hall in Prague
who: an exchange student from Brazil and a classmate
situation: Diego wants to join a history study group, though he is still learning Czech. The classmate switches to slow, clear English and hands him colour-coded notes.

place: a small seminar room in Toronto
who: a biology professor and twenty undergraduates
situation: During her five-minute talk on local bees, Priya notices her slides are stuck on a holiday photo of her dog. She keeps explaining calmly without stopping.

place: a shared flat kitchen in Berlin
who: two engineering roommates
situation: Henrik and Samir disagree loudly over who forgot to upload the final lab file before midnight. The deadline clock shows only four minutes left on the laptop.

place: the back row of a campus bus in Kyoto
who: two graduate students
situation: Kenji finally admits to Mei that he never actually read the textbook he praised in seminar. He only memorized the chapter titles on the train.

place: outside an exam hall in Dublin
who: two nervous strangers in line
situation: While waiting for the doors to open, Clara and Liam chat about the rain and their lucky pens. Neither realizes they are taking completely different exams.

place: a student union noticeboard in Leiden
who: a class representative and absent students
situation: After meeting the dean, Marta posts a short update explaining what the professor decided about the broken heating. Tomorrow's written test moves to the sports hall.

place: a computer testing centre in Sydney
who: an exam supervisor and new test-takers
situation: Before the timer starts, the supervisor explains where to leave smartwatches and how to save each answer. One student realizes his loud mechanical watch must go outside.

place: a university print shop in Lisbon
who: a thesis student and the shop assistant
situation: Eva writes a warm message to the print clerk who stayed ten minutes past closing to bind her final paper. Without his help she would have missed submission.

place: an open-plan design office in Stockholm
who: a team leader and six staff members
situation: Freya gathers everyone near the coffee machine to announce that Friday will be a paid half-day. Two colleagues drop their mugs in surprise.

place: a glass meeting booth in Chicago
who: an accountant and an impatient supplier
situation: Victor tries to solve a double-charged paper order over the phone while the office fire alarm tests beep every thirty seconds.

place: a shipping firm office in Rotterdam
who: a new clerk and a driver from Spain
situation: Carlos arrives early with forty boxes of tiles, and nobody at reception understands Spanish. The shy night security guard steps in and translates everything smoothly.

place: a bright training room in Singapore
who: an IT trainer and ten office workers
situation: Lin leads a short afternoon workshop on keeping passwords safe. Half the group laughs nervously when she mentions writing codes on yellow sticky notes under keyboards.

place: an office kitchen in Manchester
who: two marketing colleagues
situation: Owen and Rita clash over the thermostat setting and the mystery of the disappearing oat milk. Everyone else pretends to stare very seriously at the microwave.

place: a quiet office stairwell in Warsaw
who: two long-time coworkers
situation: Piotr quietly confesses to Olga that he accidentally broke the fancy espresso machine on Tuesday. He has been bringing instant coffee in a thermos all week.

place: a slow office lift in Tokyo
who: a junior analyst and the company director
situation: Stuck between floors for two minutes, Hana and the director chat politely about umbrellas and weekend bakeries. Neither mentions the urgent budget meeting they are both late for.

place: a shared project channel in Austin
who: a remote worker and her teammate
situation: After a client meeting, Tessa sends a message summarizing what the client liked and rejected. She notes that the client insisted on changing the green logo to navy blue.

place: a bakery warehouse office in Lyon
who: a shift manager and a temporary assistant
situation: Before leaving for lunch, Hugo writes clear steps for locking the delivery gate and printing afternoon labels. He underlines the rule about not unplugging the freezer alarm.

place: an architecture studio in Milan
who: a junior drafter and a senior colleague
situation: Marco accidentally sent the draft floor plan to the whole company instead of his team. He writes a quick, honest note apologizing for filling fifty inboxes.

place: a small kitchen table in Cork
who: a recent graduate and his mum
situation: Liam opens an email from the local bookstore offering him his first full-time job. He nearly knocks over the teapot rushing to share the news.

place: a noisy bus stop in Leeds
who: a job applicant and a recruitment officer
situation: Salma gets an unexpected callback for a morning interview while a street sweeper passes right behind her. She ducks into a quiet doorway to catch the office address.

place: a bright hotel lobby in Zurich
who: a front-desk candidate and the hotel manager
situation: The manager tests Nadia's French and German with a quick role-play about a missing suitcase. Nadia answers smoothly until a real guest interrupts asking for ice.

place: a community job centre in Glasgow
who: a career coach and twelve job seekers
situation: Amir gives a practical twenty-minute talk on answering tough interview questions without sounding memorized. He brings three real examples of terrible answers he once gave himself.

place: a coffee shop in Montreal
who: two co-owners of a small bike shop
situation: Chloe and David argue quietly over which candidate to hire as their mechanic. One has ten years of experience, while the other fixed their squeaky door on arrival.

place: a park bench in Vienna
who: an applicant and her close friend
situation: Petra admits she listed advanced spreadsheet skills on her CV even though she only knows basic formulas. Now the second interview includes a thirty-minute live test.

place: a reception sofa in Seattle
who: a nervous candidate and a receptionist
situation: Ten minutes before his interview, Ravi chats with the receptionist about the giant cactus on her desk. She casually mentions the manager loves short, direct answers.

place: a quiet living room in Wellington
who: a job candidate and his former manager
situation: Paul sends a message explaining what the interview panel asked about his previous warehouse role. He wants his old boss to know what they might check tomorrow.

place: an automated hiring portal email in Oslo
who: a museum coordinator and an invited candidate
situation: The museum sends clear arrival steps for the security gate and asks the candidate to bring one photo ID. Visitors must avoid the main stairs because of wet paint.

place: a sunlit home desk in Bristol
who: an unsuccessful applicant and a kind interviewer
situation: Even though he did not get the café supervisor role, Yusuf writes a polite note thanking the owner for her honest feedback about his availability.

place: a small apartment hallway in Madrid
who: a shopper and her flatmate
situation: Sara receives a text alert that her long-awaited winter coat arrived at the corner parcel locker. When she opens the box, it contains two bright yellow rain hats.

place: a sofa in a living room in Melbourne
who: a customer and an online store agent
situation: Max calls customer support because his new coffee table arrived with four legs of slightly different lengths. The agent promises a replacement before Friday.

place: a busy street market in Istanbul
who: a tourist from Poland and a spice seller
situation: Filip wants mild red pepper for his grandmother, not the hottest kind on the stall. He uses five Turkish words he practiced on the ferry, and the seller grins.

place: a local electronics shop in Antwerp
who: a store clerk and an older customer
situation: Before Vera buys a new cordless kettle, the clerk gives a quick demonstration on cleaning the metal filter and using the temperature buttons safely.

place: a return desk in a department store in Dallas
who: a customer and a store supervisor
situation: Luis insists the wool jumper shrank on its own after one cold wash. The supervisor points calmly to the bright red dry-clean-only label sewn inside the collar.

place: a family dining room in Prague
who: two teenage cousins
situation: Iris whispers to Adam that she already saw the blue bicycle hidden behind the garage curtains. She promises to act completely surprised on Saturday morning.

place: a checkout queue in a bookshop in Bath
who: two shoppers holding the same novel
situation: While waiting behind a slow card machine, Grace and a retired teacher chat about favourite mystery writers and complain gently about tiny book print.

place: an online review page for a shoe store
who: a buyer writing for other shoppers
situation: Zara posts a detailed review explaining what the delivery driver admitted when the soaked parcel arrived. The driver said the van roof had been leaking all morning.

place: a parcel pickup counter in Hamburg
who: a shop owner and a confused buyer
situation: A laminated sign beside the scanner explains how to show the six-digit pickup code and recycle cardboard boxes outside. People still keep tapping their bus cards on it.

place: a handmade pottery shop inbox in Porto
who: a ceramic artist and a patient buyer
situation: After sending a blue mug instead of a green teapot, Marta sends an immediate apology along with a prepaid return sticker and a free coaster.

place: a small regional airport in Tromso
who: a gate agent and thirty passengers
situation: Snow stops falling just in time, and the gate agent steps up to the microphone to announce that boarding will begin in ten minutes instead of tomorrow.

place: a baggage claim carousel in Frankfurt
who: a tired traveller and an airline desk clerk
situation: Omar phones the lost-luggage hotline because the only bag left on the belt looks identical to his, except for a giant sticker of a smiling banana.

place: a train ticket desk inside Rome airport
who: a Japanese traveller and a ticket clerk
situation: Kenji struggles to ask for a round-trip ticket in Italian until he switches to simple hand gestures and numbers. Both laugh when the printer spits out two perfect tickets.

place: the cabin of a narrow plane in Athens
who: a flight attendant and holiday passengers
situation: Before takeoff, the flight attendant gives the safety briefing while a nervous passenger keeps checking the life jacket pouch under his seat twice.

place: a boarding gate in London
who: a budget-airline passenger and a gate worker
situation: Tariq argues that his overstuffed backpack clearly fits inside the metal size frame. When he pushes it down, three pairs of socks pop out the side zipper.

place: a sunny café terrace near Nice airport

situation: Elena confesses to Sofia that she hates flying and always chooses the aisle seat so she never has to look out the window during takeoff.

place: a long security queue in Denver
who: two business travellers
situation: While taking off their belts and shoes, David and Priya chat about airport coffee prices and the terrible sleep they both get on night flights.

place: a crowded airport departure lounge in Bangkok
who: a traveller texting her family group
situation: Yael writes to her parents to pass on what the pilot just announced over the speaker. A flock of birds near the runway delayed takeoff by forty minutes.

place: an arrivals hall in Reykjavik
who: an information desk worker and a sleepy family
situation: The desk worker circles the purple bus stop on a map and explains how to reach the shuttle without walking through the icy car park.

place: the lost property counter in Zurich airport
who: a grateful passenger and a cleaner
situation: Leo tracks down the airport cleaner who found his passport between two café chairs and thanks him warmly with a box of Swiss chocolates.
